detail: AC5 says the registered token is still the token the Webhooks API sends with each webhook call. Only storage is checked (TC-HINT-1-14); delivery is in Open questions because it 'needs an order to reach OrderPaid on the test stack'. It doesn't: OrderStatusChangedToPaidIntegrationEventHandler only calls retriever.GetSubscriptionsOfType(OrderPaid) and sender.SendAll, and the functional fixture runs real RabbitMQ and already swaps services. Add a functional case: register (POST /api/webhooks/, X-Test-User fresh, token 'fake-token-for-tests-9z8y', url 'https://receiver.test/webhook', event OrderPaid) -> 201; publish an OrderStatusChangedToPaidIntegrationEvent (or resolve and invoke the handler) with the HttpClient primary handler replaced by a recording handler; expect exactly one POST to https://receiver.test/webhook whose X-eshop-whtoken header equals 'fake-token-for-tests-9z8y' (the full token, not its hint).

AC5 explicitly requires the entered token to be sent with webhook calls. Checking its database value does not verify the outgoing header, and this defined requirement cannot be deferred as an open question. Explicitly map reusable sender coverage, such as SenderPostsPayloadAndTokenToEveryReceiver, alongside TC-HINT-1-14, or plan an observable receiver assertion that X-eshop-whtoken equals the registered token.

The expected recorded argument and invocation count are state inside ConfigurableGrantUrlTester, not a documented public interface. Replace that assertion with an observable HTTP grant exchange: a controlled receiver verifies the exact X-eshop-whtoken header and returns the required grant response; assert POST 201 and the unchanged database token.

The Token box is clipped in the recording (shows '6168DB8D-DC58-4094…') and no caption names the token's tail, so the video cannot show that the hint '…3590' matches the typed token. The test assertion hintOf(clientToken) is correct; add a caption with the token's last 4 characters (e.g. 'Token ends in 3590') before Register. [raised by opus, sol]

The test reads clientToken from the prefilled Token box and derives its expected hint from that same value. The case explicitly requires reading WebhookClientOptions:Token from stack configuration at runtime. An incorrect nonempty prefill can therefore become both the test input and its oracle. Read the configured value independently, then fill and assert against it.

The code now adds a token-tail caption, but none of the supplied keyframes captures it. The input frame shows only the clipped prefix 6168DB8D-DC58-4094, while subsequent frames show the result …3590. Capture a keyframe with the configured token's suffix caption visible before Register so the evidence demonstrates the input-to-hint relationship.
